# Reviewed sites that read runtime digest bytes as an integer.
#
# Operator ruling A1 (2026-08-19, board DEV-772) amends standing law 2 to admit
# ONE guarded trusted-base seam: `kernelIdentity` translates a runtime content
# address into a model identity label behind a width-and-alphabet guard that
# returns a refusal carrying its law and repair, never a bare throw. A second
# translation of runtime digest bytes into identity labels anywhere under
# `packages/plait/src/` is refused.
#
# `check:kernel-door` reads every hex-prefixed `BigInt(...)` conversion under
# `src/` and requires each to be named here. This file is nothing's input:
# adding a row is the whole cost of a new site and is the diff a reviewer
# reads, and a row that stops naming a real conversion reds the wall rather
# than rotting.
#
# The rule is scoped to `BigInt` because an identity label is an unbounded
# natural. `Number.parseInt(_, 16)` yields a `number` and is structurally
# incapable of carrying a 256-bit address, so the JSON `\uXXXX` unescape in
# `truth/Canonical.ts` is not a translation this law reaches — a bound stated
# rather than a case quietly skipped.
#
# Format: <module path relative to packages/plait> <ticket>
#
# src/kernel/KernelIdentity.ts — the ruled seam itself. Its guard and its
# no-throw discipline are checked separately; this row is what makes a SECOND
# seam cost a reviewed diff rather than appearing silently beside it.
src/kernel/KernelIdentity.ts DEV-772
#
# src/planes/Lane.ts — routing, never identity. `Lane.partition` reduces an
# already-branded `Digest` modulo the declared partition count to pick a shard;
# the result is a routing coordinate that reaches no candidate and names no
# declaration. It carries the same syntax as the seam and so must be seen by
# the wall rather than exempted, and the package's own law already governs it:
# subjects route and envelopes identify.
src/planes/Lane.ts DEV-772
